From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Bates <oliver.bates@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime usage limits & output title — MSA/Order Form redline coordination

Oliver — attaching the latest redline for the Order Form and a short summary of the open IP/runtime items we expect will need agreement before procurement can sign:

1) Output title: Acme has proposed assignment of "Output title" in the Order Form. We're pushing back to preserve standard Redwood pattern (customer title to Customer Content and Output; Redwood retains a service delivery license).

2) Training & feedback license: current ACME redline would permit broader use of customer-provided outputs for model retraining. We propose a narrower, opt-in feedback license: Redwood may use aggregated/anonymous feedback for model quality improvements but not to retrain models that are productized or sold back to customers without explicit consent.

3) Runtime/embedded assets: Acme asked for rights to host our runtime in their VPC and persist embeddings generated by Redwood. We need clear limits on persist/redistribute; suggest limiting embedding persistence to customer-owned containers and requiring contractual prohibitions on publishing training datasets derived from outputs.

4) Telemetry & logs: propose telemetry allowed for performance/operational debugging but with PII filters and retention capped at 90 days unless otherwise agreed in SOC 2/audit scope.

Key ask: can you and Laura take a quick pass on the attached redline and let me know which items you're comfortable conceding vs. what we should escalate to legal? Target: respond to Acme by EOD Monday with a consolidated position.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline of Order Form), redline_clause_suggestions.docx (internal notes)

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Runtime usage limits & output title — MSA/Order Form redline coordination

Karthik — thanks for the packet. A few quick clarifying questions from our legal/ops side after a first pass:

- On "Output title": Acme's intent is pragmatic — we need to ensure downstream product teams can ship features that incorporate generated output without re-asking for rights. Assignment is the cleanest path; would Redwood accept a limited assignment for "Productized Outputs" (features shipped to end users) while allowing Redwood audit/telemetry rights?

- Training vs. quality improvements: can you draw a line for us between "quality improvements" and "retraining for productization"? If we get carveouts for very specific models/cases, we can be flexible.

- Embedded artifacts / VPC: we are sensitive about vendor-hosted persistence of embeddings for regulated workflows. If we host embeddings, ACME could accept a data-processing addendum that allows Redwood to cache transiently for performance.

Attached is our team's updated PDF with marginal notes and a couple of proposed edits inline.

Can we hop on a 20-min call Monday to align before legal trades redlines?

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Bates | Head of Product Partnerships, Acme Corp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Runtime usage limits & output title — suggested negotiation positions

Team — forwarding Acme's response. My read and proposed middle-ground language below (I'll call out line items so legal can reuse):

1) Output title: propose we accept "Customer retains title to Output; Redwood receives perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Output to provide the Services and for internal analytics and debugging. Productization (i.e., selling the Output or embedding it in a standalone Redwood product) requires Customer opt-in and an express limited license."

2) Training & feedback license: propose a two-tier approach — (A) telemetry/aggregated logs: Redwood may use anonymized telemetry and aggregate signals to improve model routing and performance; (B) model retraining/productization: Redwood may only use Customer Output for retraining if Customer opts into a separate training license (opt-in checkbox on Order Form). No default assignment of rights for training.

3) Embedding persistence: if Acme hosts embeddings in their VPC, we accept that but require contractual prohibition on using persisted embeddings to retrain models or externalize them. If Redwood persists embeddings for performance, it will be encrypted, associated with the customer's tenant, and only used for caching/latency improvements unless a separate agreement is reached.

4) Telemetry retention: 90 days default; 12 months max with justification and SOC2 evidence.

Next steps: Laura — can you convert the bullets above into redline-ready clauses? Aditya — please validate operational feasibility with infra (embedding caching, key rotation, retention windows). I want a short reply to Acme by EOD tomorrow.

Karthik

Karthik / team — tagging in some pragmatic contract language you can paste into the Order Form. High-level approach: (1) be prescriptive about definitions, (2) keep training usage opt-in, (3) allow telemetry for quality/ops with strict anonymization. Suggested snippets below — legal has reviewed this draft and is comfortable advancing with the positions. Please confirm you can operationalize the telemetry/retention items.

Suggested definitions snippet:
"Customer Content": any data, prompts, inputs, and uploaded files provided by Customer.
"Output": text, embeddings, and other artifacts generated by the Service in response to Customer Content.

Suggested clauses (paste-ready):
- Output Ownership: "Customer retains title to Output. Subject to that, Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use Output solely to provide the Services and for anonymized analytics and operational debugging. Redwood shall not use Output to train or improve models that are productized and sold to third parties without Customer's prior written consent.

- Feedback & Training License (opt-in): "Customer may opt in to a separate 'Training License' that permits Redwood to use Customer Content and Output to retrain or fine-tune models. Absent such opt-in, Redwood will not use Customer Content or Output for model training beyond aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement."

- Embeddings & Persistence: "If Customer elects to persist embeddings in Customer-managed infrastructure, Redwood will not retain a copy for more than 24 hours except for transient caching to serve low-latency requests. Any persistence by Redwood will be tenant-scoped, encrypted at rest, and used only for caching and latency improvements unless the parties execute a separate agreement."

- Telemetry & Retention: "Operational telemetry (latency, error rates, resource usage) may be retained up to 90 days. Debugging traces that may contain PII or Customer Content will be redacted and retained only as necessary and subject to the Data Processing Addendum."

I attached a DOCX with these snippets so legal can push a clean tracked-change back to ACME. If Aditya confirms infra is OK, I can send to ACME Contracts with the suggested compromise language.

Attachment: redline_clause_suggestions.docx

Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Soojin — thanks for the quick turnaround and proposed language. Our legal team reviewed and is broadly comfortable with the opt-in training license approach. Two remaining asks before we can issue a DocuSign package:

1) Narrower "Productization" definition: please replace the parenthetical with an explicit definition — e.g., 'Productization means (a) bundling Output into a standalone product or feature that is licensed or sold to third parties; or (b) using Output to train models which are subsequently offered to customers as a product.'

2) Evidence & audit: Acme requires a one-time evidence package that shows telemetry anonymization and retention practices (SOC2 controls + architecture diagram) prior to signature.

If you can confirm acceptance of those two items and send a DocuSign-ready MSA + Order Form redline, we will route for signature on Acme's side. Also propose a short call Thursday 30 minutes to finalize the definitions.

Regards,
Acme Contracts Team
